findings.title: AppLifecycleGuardTest never proves its STOPPING-state guard checks ran; onStop swallows any non-ISE failure
findings.description: sdsAc3 runs rejectAll(...) inside app.onStart/app.onStop callbacks (lines 105-106) and only checks that the collected `problems` list is empty (line 111). rejectAll catches only IllegalStateException. In STOPPING, an exception thrown from an onStop callback is logged and swallowed by the shutdown sequence (see AppIsolationTest, where a throwing onStop is only logged), so a regression where e.g. `post("/n", null, H)` throws NullPointerException before the lifecycle guard (the exact ordering the test claims to pin at line 58), or where a guarded method simply stops throwing inside the callback after the first accepted call, leaves `problems` empty and the test green. There is also no assertion that the onStop (or onStart) callback executed at all (no counter), so the STARTING/STOPPING rows of FR-APP-002 AC-3 are unverified; only RUNNING and TERMINATED are checked from the test thread.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a per-state invocation marker (e.g. an AtomicInteger/EnumSet of states reached) in the callbacks and assert STARTING and STOPPING were both visited; catch Throwable in rejectAll and add non-ISE failures to `problems` so they cannot be swallowed by the lifecycle error logging.

findings.title: sdsAc2_IR_HTTP_001_AC3_laterWaveMethodNamesAreAbsent is vacuous
findings.description: LATER_WAVE_NAMES is Collections.<String>emptyList() (line 32), so the loop at lines 228-232 asserts `emptyList().contains(name)` is false for every Request/Response method; it can never fail. The test name and the SDS reference still advertise a guard that no longer exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the test and the constant (the exact-signature sets in the neighbouring tests already pin the surface), or give it a real forbidden-name list.

findings.title: Negative assertions use a fixed sleep/poll window that hides late extra log lines and callbacks
findings.description: AccessLogAcceptanceTest:237 sleeps 50 ms and then asserts exactly 2 log lines ("a line from onDone would follow the close line at once"); DispatcherTest:605 repeats the same 5+50 ms pattern. The defect these guard against (a duplicate access line written by onDone on another thread) passes both tests whenever the extra line lands later than 50 ms, e.g. on a loaded CI box. Likewise DefaultWebSocketSessionTest:115,137,212,251,279 and HttpAdapterSpiTest:146 assert "nothing else happens" with events.poll(200 ms)/get(150 ms) timeouts. These are false-pass (not flaky-fail) windows.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the extra event observable deterministically: e.g. flush the adapter/exchange to its terminal state (session TERMINATED, adapter.release()) before reading the log, or have RecordingLogger expose a latch that is counted down after the last expected writer finished, and assert the count once after that point.

findings.title: Wall-clock upper bounds in SPI and access-log tests are timing dependent
findings.description: sdsAc6 asserts adapter.stop(100 ms) took `elapsedMs >= 90 && elapsedMs < 2000` and adapter.release() returns in <= 1500 ms. On a CPU-starved or GC-paused CI worker the 2 s / 1.5 s ceilings are exceeded without any defect (reproducible under -Dtest parallelism or a stop-the-world pause). AccessLogAcceptanceTest:311-322 also compares the logged `sse start=` epoch with two System.currentTimeMillis() reads, which breaks if the wall clock steps backwards between them.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the upper bounds (keep only the lower bound proving the deadline was honoured) or raise them to a generous multiple; for the epoch check use `start >= before - slack`.

findings.title: SPI tests hard-code the module jar name and version
findings.description: sdsAc7 requires the SPI classes to come from `.../NaruServe-api/build/classes/java/main` or a jar ending in `NaruServe-api-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` (lines 305-306); the sibling check at lines 334-335 uses a different, version-agnostic regex. build.gradle line 23 owns the version (`0.1.0-SNAPSHOT`), so bumping it for a release (the window adds release tooling, -Prelease) makes this test fail although nothing is wrong, and a checkout directory not named NaruServe-api also fails it.
findings.suggested_fix: Reuse the regex form of line 335 (`NaruServe-api-[^/]*\.jar`) or assert only that the code source is not under src/testFixtures or the test output.

findings.title: CallbackMatrixKotlinTest depends on method order and static state shared between tests
findings.description: The final test `z every CALLBACK_TYPES interface was exercised` (line 189-191) passes only if all of a..e already ran in the same JVM and class (shared companion `exercised`, @FixMethodOrder(NAME_ASCENDING)). Running it alone (IDE re-run of a single test, `gradle test --tests "*CallbackMatrixKotlinTest.*z*"`) or any earlier failure before a `hit(...)` call makes it fail with a misleading set difference, and it would break under parallel method execution.
findings.suggested_fix: Compute the exercised set in a single test, or use a @ClassRule/@AfterClass assertion that is skipped when fewer than all tests ran, instead of a test that relies on ordering.

findings.title: Tests leave files in the system temp dir via createTempFile + deleteOnExit
findings.description: DefaultUploadFileTest.assertContentGone creates `File.createTempFile("dest", ".bin")` on every call (invoked about ten times per run) and relies on deleteOnExit, so the files persist for the life of the test JVM and accumulate in the deleteOnExit registry; a killed Gradle worker leaves them forever. HttpAdapterSpiTest:165-166 does the same. The class already has a TemporaryFolder rule that would clean up deterministically.
findings.suggested_fix: Create the destination with tmp.newFile() (instance rule is not available in the static helper, so pass the File in) and drop deleteOnExit.

findings.title: Docs tests resolve ../docs/api from user.dir, inconsistent with other tests that also accept the repo root
findings.description: HttpDocsTest.doc (used by AppDocsTest and ten other test methods) and DefaultMimeTypesTest:50 open `new File(user.dir, "../docs/api/...")`; they throw FileNotFoundException when the test JVM starts in the repository root (IDE default working directory), while CookieParserTest:86-90, DefaultRestAppTest:257-261 and HttpAdapterSpiTest.checkoutRoot handle both layouts. Failure shows up as an IOException rather than an assertion, which hides what was being verified.
findings.suggested_fix: Share one helper that tries `docs/api` then `../docs/api` (as checkoutRoot does) and use it from all docs tests.

findings.title: ConsoleLoggerTest swaps process-global System.out/err, TimeZone and Locale while other threads may still log
findings.description: redirect() replaces System.out/System.err for the whole JVM and several tests call TimeZone.setDefault / Locale.setDefault. Other tests in the module leave live daemon threads (InMemoryHttpAdapter workers, WebSocket sender threads, drain threads) and construct ConsoleLogger instances (DefaultResponseTest.registry, DefaultSseClientTest.registry); any of them writing a WARN/INFO line while a ConsoleLoggerTest case runs lands in the captured `out`/`err`, so assertions such as `assertEquals(o.toString(), 1, o.size())` (line 125) fail intermittently. The restore in @After is correct but does not remove the window.
findings.suggested_fix: Test ConsoleLogger.format and the write path against an injectable PrintStream, or run this class in its own fork (forkEvery) / filter captured lines by the test message prefix.
